questions.q: What is a Terraform workspace, according to this lesson?
options: A feature that only exists inside Terraform Cloud, not the open-source CLI
A separate copy of the entire configuration directory for each environment
A named state file within one backend, tied to the same configuration — not a separate copy of the .tf files
A folder that stores provider plugin binaries
questions.explain: A workspace keeps an independent state file for the same HCL configuration — the .tf files never change, only which state plan/apply read from and write to.

questions.q: What workspace is a Terraform working directory in before you ever run terraform workspace new?
options: local
There is no workspace until one is explicitly created
prod
default
questions.explain: Every working directory starts in a workspace literally named default, used automatically even if you never type the word.

questions.q: What does terraform workspace select staging do?
options: Deletes the staging workspace
Runs terraform apply against the staging workspace immediately
Switches the active workspace to staging without creating a new one
Creates a brand-new workspace named staging
questions.explain: select switches between existing workspaces; new is the command that creates one. select is the command to run before every plan/apply to confirm you're pointed at the right environment.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what does terraform.workspace let a configuration do?
options: Automatically create a new workspace every time apply runs
Change which cloud provider the configuration deploys to
Vary resource naming and sizing (e.g. VM size via a lookup map) based on the active workspace's name
Replace the need for a required_providers block
questions.explain: terraform.workspace is a built-in, readable value — the example uses it both in a resource group name and as the lookup key into a VM-size map.

questions.q: What do all workspaces in a configuration still share, which is the real limitation of the workspace approach?
options: The same exact state file
The same terraform.workspace value at all times
Nothing — each workspace has fully isolated credentials and permissions by default
The same backend, the same provider block, and typically the same credentials
questions.explain: Workspaces share backend, provider configuration, and usually credentials, which means nothing technically prevents applying to the wrong environment by mistake.
